domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n > 1
k ranges over integers with 1 <= k <= n (implicit from the sum)
frac(x) is defined as x minus floor(x), so frac(x) lies in the interval from 0 up to but not including 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n greater than 1, define f_n on real numbers by f_n(x) equals floor of n times x minus the sum from k equals 1 to n of (floor of k times x divided by k). Then for every real x, f_n(x) equals f_n(frac(x)), where frac(x) equals x minus floor(x).
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n > 1

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter for the function f_n; assumed greater than 1

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index inside the definition of f_n

variables.name: x
variables.role: input variable to the function f_n

variables.name: f_n
variables.role: value defined from n and floor expressions

variables.name: frac(x)
variables.role: auxiliary transform defined as x minus floor(x)

witness_dependencies: no existential witnesses; f_n is uniquely determined by n

statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and let f_n be defined by f_n(x) = floor(n*x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k*x)/k. For every real x, f_n(x) = f_n(frac(x)), where frac(x) = x - floor(x).
